info.name: fi-idp-mock - APIs to test (case-insensitive)
info.description:
Clean list of fi-idp-mock API requests to test. NOT case-specific: POST /connect/token lowercases the username before lookup, so FATEMA / FaTeMa / fatema all target the same account (the password must still match the seed). Only real APIs are listed here; the deprecated /mint backdoor is intentionally excluded (see README 'Endpoints').

Run the mock first: docker compose up --build  (Dhaka Bank on :5105, EBL on :5106)
  or: FI_ID=dhakabank PORT=5105 node src/server.js

This collection is a plain listing of APIs to poke — no pm.test assertion scripts, no pass/fail scenarios. Error behaviour (invalid_grant, account_locked, password_expired, unsupported_grant_type) is documented in services/fi-idp-mock/README.md under 'POST /connect/token'.

variable.description: Dhaka Bank mock. Switch to http://localhost:5106 for EBL via eblBaseUrl.
Paste a refresh_token obtained from a password-grant login (items 04-06) to use in the refresh request (item 07).

request.description: GET /health — liveness probe. Expect 200 { status, fi_id, fi_name, issuer, users }.
GET /.well-known/openid-configuration — OIDC discovery. Expect 200 with issuer, jwks_uri, token_endpoint, grant_types_supported (password, refresh_token), scopes_supported and claims_supported.
GET /.well-known/jwks.json — RSA public signing key. Expect 200 { keys: [ { kid, alg: 'RS256', ... } ] }.

POST /connect/token — password grant (active user, lowercase seed username). Expect 200 { access_token, id_token, refresh_token, token_type: 'Bearer', expires_in, scope, refresh_expires_in }. access_token sub = 'user-fatema'.
NOT case-specific: UPPERCASE username 'FATEMA' resolves to the same fatema account as item 04. Expect 200, access_token sub = 'user-fatema' (lowercased).
NOT case-specific: MixedCase username 'FaTeMa' resolves to the same fatema account. Expect 200, access_token sub = 'user-fatema'.

POST /connect/token — refresh grant. Set {{refresh_token}} (from item 04/05/06) first. Expect 200 with a fresh access_token + new refresh_token; the old refresh_token is rotated (reusing it returns 400 invalid_grant).
Only password and refresh_token grants are supported. Expect 400 { error: 'unsupported_grant_type' }.
